121	Tamuz. Sivan is the third month in the count
122	of the months; the first month is Nisan, so
123	Sivan is the third month. The letter connected with
124	the number three is the letter
125	Gimel. Tamuz is the fourth of the
126	months. The letter connected with Tamuz is the letter
127	Dalet. And as we pass from Sivan to Tamuz, on Shabbat
128	we bless, G-d willing, tomorrow in the synagogue,
129	after the Torah reading, we will bless Rosh Chodesh
130	Tamuz, which comes upon us for good, which falls, G-d willing,
131	on Rosh Chodesh Tamuz, which comes upon us for good, which falls on the day of
132	the holy Shabbat and the next day, Sunday, and not after it. So
133	the blessing is really a kind of drawing down and giving of strength
134	from this Shabbat, and from our presence now in the month of Sivan,
135	to the month of Tamuz, the coming month. That is, there is here
136	a connection between the Gimel
137	and the Dalet. The Sages say: what is the hint in the letters?
138	Gimel, Dalet:
139	"gomel dalim." Gimel comes from the word gomel, which is really the act of
140	the giver,
141	the one who bestows. And so too with the letters of the Holy Tongue, everything is
142	precisely exact. The shape of the letter Gimel in the Holy Tongue
143	is like a Vav that has a hand
144	stretched out. It is like the giver who extends his hand. Toward where does he extend his hand? Toward the letter
145	that follows.
146	Toward the Dalet. The letter Dalet, by contrast,
147	is just as it sounds. Just as Gimel is gomel, so Dalet
148	comes from the word dal, poor. The gomel gives to the one who has nothing,
149	to the dal. And how do I know that the Dalet receives from the Gimel? Because the dal
150	extends a hand toward the Gimel. Where is the hand of the Dalet? The
151	Dalet is like the letter
152	Resh. But the Resh has no hand; the Resh has pride, it
153	does not want to receive from anyone. Not so the Dalet, which
154	extends a hand to the Gimel to receive
155	the bestowal. And when the bestowal passes from the Gimel to the Dalet, really
156	the power of the third month, which is the power of the Torah,
157	the light of the Torah, descends below, to the world, for this world
158	is
159	divided into four. Why is the world divided into four? The Torah is connected
160	with the Gimel. The Torah has Torah, Prophets
161	and Writings. The Torah was given to us in the third month,
162	on the third day, through the third one, who is Moshe
163	Rabbeinu. It was given to the people of Israel, who are divided into three:
164	Kohanim, Levites and Israelites. In the letters of the Torah there are
165	three kinds of letters: large letters,
166	medium letters, and small letters,
167	and there are many more matters of three in the Torah.
168	The whole Torah revolves around the matter of three,
169	because the matter of three is the matter of peace,
170	of strength. Shalom is also the numerical value of "chazakah," but in the context
171	of ours now, the whole Torah was given to make peace
172	in the world. Dispute began on the second day, and this is exactly the power of
173	the third, which brings the power of peace to make
174	peace between the two, the dispute between the two. For how does the Torah
175	make peace? Right, how does the Torah make peace?
176	Since the Torah is the wisdom of HaShem and becomes one
177	with HaShem, when you reveal the power of
178	the Holy One, blessed be He, in every
179	situation, suddenly you notice that although
180	there can be enormous disputes between Beit Hillel
181	and Beit Shammai, not to mention that those were disputes for the sake of
182	Heaven, not to mention other disputes, where is there room
183	for dispute? When
184	we are speaking
185	of the mind of the lower human being, whose mind, since
186	it is limited, can grasp things
187	in a very particular way, and just as their faces are not
188	alike, so their opinions are not alike. So in opinion there can
189	be dispute. But the moment they reveal the mind of
190	the Torah, that the Torah reveals HaShem, then automatically
191	peace is made. Therefore the whole Torah is connected with the number
192	three, which is the power to make peace between the two
193	who are in dispute
194	with each other. But this Torah, from its power to make
195	peace, being connected with HaShem, already teaches
196	us that it is not at the level of the world; it is above
197	the world. The Torah preceded the world by 2000 years.
198	And in order for the Torah to reach the world, the Jew must
199	bring the Torah down from the number three to the number
200	four. Why is the number four connected with the world? Because
201	the world was created in such a way that it has time and place,
202	and the reality of place is divided into four directions, the four
203	directions
204	of the heavens. The whole world is divided into four kinds. What
205	are the four kinds
206	of the world?
207	Inanimate, vegetative, animal,
208	and speaking. Also spiritually, and in Kabbalah, we
209	know that the world HaShem created is divided into four
210	worlds: Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah,
211	and Asiyah. In the world there are also four elements: fire, wind,
212	water, and earth. This is connected to those four levels, yes:
213	the inanimate is earth, the last element, the lowest
214	of all, and above it is water, which is connected to the vegetative;
215	water makes all kinds of things grow,
216	pleasure; and wind is the spirit of the animal soul of
217	living creatures; and fire belongs to the speaking, the highest level
218	of the speaking, which has the ability to connect
219	with the soul, which is also called flames of fire, like
220	a spiritual flame that HaShem implanted in the lower man so that
221	he could cleave to holiness
222	and so on. So
223	if so, the world is divided into four, but so that this world
224	will not conceal and hide the reality of HaShem, as HaShem
225	created it to be so, not through its own fault, HaShem created
226	the world to be concealing
227	and hiding, HaShem gave the Jew in parallel the
228	Torah, for the Gimel is the power of the three, to
229	bring peace to the world. And how do we make peace? As
230	we said before, by revealing HaShem,
231	He who makes peace in His heights will make peace
232	upon us. That is, the same peace made in the heights
233	between the camp of Michael on the side of Chesed and the camp of Gavriel on the side of
234	Gevurah is made upon us and upon all Israel when
235	we engage in Torah and bring peace
236	to the world. The whole Torah was given to make peace in the world.
